title: THE GENERATION THAT WAS ONLY THE MIDDLE
deck: Long Vesper is two hundred and six years into a four-hundred-year crossing, and the people who keep it alive have stopped lifting a hand beyond the minimum. A dust drift is forty-one days away. Illuminara works the hated shifts before she asks for anything.
shape: Eight scenes across forty-one days and a morning after: a failing apron, six shifts in the grit, a hearing on the assembly floor, a night in the maintenance bay, a captain's day room, a compost bay that keeps a ledger, the day the drift arrives, and a hill with a bench on it.

scenes.title: The Scour
paragraphs: *Long Vesper, Ring One, the Scour gantry · forty-one days before the drift, 06:00 ship-time*

The dust had been sanding the front of the ship for two hundred and six years, and it showed in the way the maintenance chief crossed the gantry: carefully, as if the floor might have an opinion. Soren Kalu was a narrow man in a coverall gone white at the knees, and he held his tablet against his chest the way people hold something that has been ill.

Below the viewport lay the apron, a slab of ice and sintered rock a kilometre across, riding ahead of the ship to take whatever the dark threw at it. The plans asked for thirty metres. In the work light it measured nineteen.

**Soren**  
Forty-one days. A drift of ice and grit, a week wide, crossing our line at full speed. It opens Rings One, Two and Three to the dark: eleven thousand people. Four hundred and twelve are on my hull crews, and for fourteen months they have done the minimum and not one plate more.

**Illuminara**  
Have you asked them?

**Soren**  
I have asked. I have ordered. They say *yes, chief,* and the plate stays in the rack.

**Illuminara**  
I can brace one section of hull for an hour, if I know where, and I will not pretend it is more. I cannot hold a kilometre of apron for forty-one nights, and I cannot make a generation care about a place it will never see. I would like to know what they do care about.

**Soren**  
They will tell you nothing. That is what fourteen months sounds like.

**Illuminara**  
Then I won't start with questions. Which shift do they hate most?

**Soren**  
The apron face. Eleven hours outside, scraping pits out of the ice with a hand tool. We draw lots.

**Illuminara**  
Put me on the rota under the same name as everyone else. I will take the draw as it falls.
Soren looked at her as if she had asked him to wind a clock backwards. Then he wrote her name in the margin of the rota, in pencil.

scenes.title: Six Shifts
paragraphs: *The apron face, outer lock Two · thirty-eight days before the drift, third shift*

By the third shift her gloves had worn through at the thumbs and she had stopped apologising to the tool. The grit hissed across her visor like rain on a tin roof. She scraped, and moved, and scraped, a metre of ice at a time, behind a woman named Mato Ibarra, a welder and crew chief, small and wide, with forearms like cable, who had worked the face for twenty years and had so far said four words to her. *Left. Lower. No. Again.* Her crew did what the rota said, and when the rota ended they went home.
In the fourth hour the seam let go.

A patch plate the size of a door, laid two generations ago, came up off the old weld with a sound Illuminara felt in her teeth. Behind it lay Ring One's outer skin and, behind that, a corridor where a hundred people were asleep. Three of the crew went for the plate's edges. Mato went for the weld.

Illuminara put both hands flat on the plate and let the load run through her, down her arms and into the frame, the way she had once held a corridor open between two habitats. It was small and hard and precise, and she did not tell herself it was small. The plate stopped moving. Mato knelt under it and ran her glove along the failed seam without looking, and found the old bead by touch, the way a pianist finds a note in the dark.

**Mato**  
Third pass is cold. Someone laid it too fast. Hold.

**Illuminara**  
Holding.
It took four minutes. When the new bead was down, Mato sat back on her heels and looked at the plate for a long moment.

**Mato**  
My mother laid the repair on that seam in her forty-fourth year. I was nine. I held the torch. Some part of me wanted it to hold.
She did not say thank you. She handed Illuminara the scraper back.

By the sixth shift Illuminara had asked eleven crew chiefs the same thing, in the lock, over tea from a flask: *If this voyage were not yours to maintain, what would you build?* Ten of them looked at her as if she were being cruel. The eleventh was Mato.

**Mato**  
A hill.

**Illuminara**  
A hill?

**Mato**  
Something that gets taller when you leave it alone. My aunt keeps goats on the spoil heaps behind Ring Seven. Sedge knits the dust and the droppings into a mat you can bounce on, and every year the heap is a little more. It is not soil. It is what soil would be if anyone left it alone. We scrape this ice every day and every day it is the same ice. I would like one thing on this ship that is more tomorrow than it was today. I would like to sit on it.

**Mato**  
Don't tell the delegates. They will make it a motion.
Illuminara's palms had blistered through two layers of glove, and she was laughing, quietly, at being outranked by a welder. It was the best she had felt in a month. She did not stop to ask why.

scenes.title: The Floor
paragraphs: *Ring Four, the assembly floor · thirty-three days before the drift, 19:00*
Four hundred people filled the floor and the tiers above it, and none of them made a sound while the Captain spoke.

Imre Dalca was sixty, spare and upright, with the ship's gold bars on a collar worn soft. He read from a page. From the first of the month, hull-hours would be tied to ration cards: any crew that missed quota would lose a tenth of its allocation until quota was met. The drift was real, he said, and so was the law, and on a ship one person's silence could be another's death.
Nobody shouted. That was what Illuminara noticed. Four hundred people sat with their hands in their laps and looked at him with the courteous blankness of people who had already decided.
Then Rina Okonkwo-Wells stood up in the second tier. Ring Four's delegate was forty-five and broad, with a voice she used like a trowel.

**Rina**  
Captain, we heard the order. May I put a question to your guest instead?

**Dalca**  
The floor is yours.

**Rina**  
She has worked six shifts on the apron face. My cousin was on the third, and says the visitor holds a plate like she means it. So I will ask her what I cannot ask you. You want us to risk our hands for people on a planet we will never see. Who ever built something for us to arrive in?
Illuminara found she had no answer ready, and understood that this was the first honest question anyone had asked her in a month.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody. I don't think anybody did.
A ripple went through the tiers, not quite a laugh.

**Illuminara**  
You were born between a leaving you did not choose and an arrival you will not see. You have kept this ship alive for two hundred years with your hands, and nobody wrote that down anywhere either. I don't think you are refusing the work. I think you are refusing work with no finish line inside one life.

**Rina**  
That is a speech. I have heard speeches. What do you do with it?

**Illuminara**  
Ask. I asked eleven crew chiefs what they would build if the voyage were not theirs to maintain. Ten would not answer me. One did.
She did not say the name. Across the floor Mato Ibarra had gone very still.

**Rina**  
Then here is what I will give you. Three days. Find me something a woman of thirty-one can begin and a woman of sixty can finish, and I will put it to my ring. If you cannot, the drift is yours to explain to my people. They will not hear it from him.

**Dalca**  
And if she cannot, Delegate, I enforce the order.

**Rina**  
Then we will both have learned something about this ship, Captain.

scenes.title: Tonnes
paragraphs: *Maintenance bay Nine · thirty-one days before the drift, 02:10*

Mato had come to the bay at midnight with a rota sheet folded in four and a rag-wrapped lump in her coverall pocket. She smoothed the sheet on Soren's bench. On the back, in welder's pencil, was a drawing: a long low rise against the ship's side, a path winding up it, and three small stick figures at the top, sitting down.

**Soren**  
That is a berm.

**Mato**  
That is a hill.

**Soren**  
It is a pile of regolith with nothing on it. Where would it go? Who would carry it? In thirty days?

**Illuminara**  
Soren. What is the apron made of?

**Soren**  
Ice and sintered rock, laid in lifts a metre at a time. Every forty years the crews strip what the dust has eaten and lay new, and the spent layers go over the side. You can read the log. It is the most boring document on the ship.

She had not read it. He handed it over with the pity he reserved for the curious, and she read it standing. *Spent apron, year 120: thirty-one thousand tonnes. Year 160: thirty-four. Disposition: space.* A column of figures that ended, every time, in the same word.

**Illuminara**  
This is the mass of a hill. Every forty years this ship lays a hill and throws it away. What if the next lift were laid as a hill, and kept?
He stared at her. Then he took the pencil out of Mato's fingers without asking and began to write beside the drawing: tonnes, layers, impact depth.

**Soren**  
Loose regolith strips like a dry riverbank. It would need a binder.

**Mato**  
Sod.

**Soren**  
What?
Mato unwrapped the rag. In it lay a square of knit sedge the size of a book, cut from her aunt's heap, its underside a dark felt of roots.

**Mato**  
Cut it, roots and all, a hand thick. A mat is a net. Grit goes into it and does not come out.
Soren held the square in the bench blower's jet for ten minutes with grit from the gantry sump, turning it. Then he weighed it on the bench balance and was silent for three breaths.

**Soren**  
It lost nothing. A plate would have lost a skin. Three lifts, nine or ten days each, with a hand of compost under every sod so the roots reach down in days, not seasons. The sods are cut and cured ahead of each lift, so the work on the apron is only the laying. Ice from Ring Five's reserve. Compost from the only two places this ship keeps real soil, the grain bays of Five and Six. Six percent of the rations for three seasons, and it gets better every year after, which no plate apron ever did.

**Illuminara**  
Who decides about the bays?

**Soren**  
Five. Six. And the Captain's ration board, which has lent itself the soil before.
She looked at the three stick figures on the hill. She had found the shape of a solution and could do nothing with it; every piece of it was somebody else's to give.

**Illuminara**  
Then it isn't mine yet. It is Mato's drawing and your arithmetic. It belongs to the people who will pay for it.

scenes.title: A Ship That Votes
paragraphs: *The Captain's day room, Ring Two · thirty days before the drift, 08:00*

Dalca received them standing. Illuminara had asked for the meeting with Rina beside her, and he had agreed with the face of a man swallowing something he would have sent back. On his desk, on a small stand, sat an old brass valve handle with no label.
Rina laid out the hill. Soren laid out the tonnes. The Captain listened without interrupting, and at the end he sat down.

**Dalca**  
A garden. I order a shield rebuilt and you bring me a garden.

**Rina**  
We bring you a shield that is also a garden, Captain. The tonnes are the same.

**Dalca**  
And when a ring council votes to stop laying it on day twenty because it is raining on somebody's wedding? A ship that votes on its shield is a ship that can vote not to have one.
Rina opened her mouth. Illuminara touched her sleeve, a very small thing, and Rina closed it again.

**Illuminara**  
What is the valve?
Dalca looked at the brass as if he had forgotten it was there.

**Dalca**  
Ring Three, year one hundred and thirty-one. The Refusal. A quarrel over water shares, and the ring's crew stopped the scrubber cycle for six days to make a point. Nineteen people in the upper tiers died of thin air before the vote reached the lower ones. My grandmother was one. This is the valve they were told to turn, and did not. It sits on my desk so that nobody has to explain to me what a ship that says no looks like.
Nobody spoke.

**Illuminara**  
Then you are not afraid of the Middle. You are afraid of the one thing a ship cannot survive them refusing.

**Dalca**  
Yes.

**Illuminara**  
Then write that down. Not as an order. As a clause.
Rina was already pulling a stylus from her sleeve.

**Rina**  
Air, water, hull. No council, no ring, no delegate may stop them or vote them down. Not for a quarrel, not for a wedding. Written into the charter by the Middle and signed by every delegate. We put the Ring Three number on the first line.
Dalca read it twice. He did not look relieved. He looked like a man who had been handed something heavy and honest.

**Dalca**  
And in return?

**Rina**  
The Garden is ours: its labour, its hours, its layout. Your authority covers hull safety, as it does now, and lapses when the emergency does. And the board does not take the grain bays back the next time it is cross.

**Dalca**  
The board has borrowed from those bays before. I will not pretend otherwise. Whatever number Ring Six writes, the board pays, out of its share of the recycler's yield, before any table. That share is mine to allot. Put it in.
Rina wrote it in.

**Illuminara**  
And the cards?

**Dalca**  
A ration card is the one lever I own that needs no one to be willing. That is why I reached for it. It is the lever the Ring Three crew pulled, only pulled from my side. Soren. Strike the cards from the hull-hours. Today.

**Soren**  
Yes, Captain.
The Captain stood. He picked up the valve and set it down again, a quarter-turn from where it had been.

**Dalca**  
I do not like it. I will sign it, because the Ring Three clause is in it. Not because anyone asked me to trust the Middle.

**Rina**  
We did not ask. We wrote you something you can check. It is not a charter until Ring Six has read it. Six keeps the second bay, and Six is the Hollow Watch.

**Dalca**  
Then go and be refused.

scenes.title: The Second Bay
paragraphs: *Ring Six, bay Two · twenty-nine days before the drift, 07:40*

The Hollow Watch were waiting: eleven people in grey smocks along a rail above the compost beds, saying nothing in the exact manner of people who had said it all before. The bay smelled of warm earth, the only warm earth on the ship. Illuminara had not known how much she missed the smell until it was in her throat.
Edda Voss kept the bay. She was seventy-one and wore her years like a tool belt, and she held a paper ledger against her ribs with both hands.

**Rina**  
Every ring has read the charter but yours, Edda. The Captain has said he will sign.

**Edda**  
I have read it. It says the board may not take the bays back when it is cross. It does not say who gives them back when you are finished.

**Rina**  
Nobody is taking anything. It is a loan.

**Edda**  
Is it. Come here, stranger.
She opened the ledger on the rail. Two columns ran down every page, in the same hand, then a younger one, then hers.

**Edda**  
Soil is the one thing this ship cannot make. We make it by letting things die in the dark for ninety years. Four times someone has come for a season's worth: hull, in year one hundred and fifteen; the reactor shield; the water works; the blight year. Every time the people asking were frightened and the cause was good, and a tonne went out through the lock, and I wrote it here. Lent, two hundred and twelve tonnes. This is the column for what came back.
The second column was empty from the top of the page to the bottom.

**Illuminara**  
Why did you keep lending?

**Edda**  
Because a debt nobody enters is a gift, and nobody thanks you for a gift you were not asked to give.
Illuminara thought of the apron log, whose column ended every time in a single word. Soren's ship threw mass away without a name. Edda's lent it without one.

**Illuminara**  
The Captain's log ends every line with *space.* Yours ends with nothing. It is the same column.

**Edda**  
Pretty. Pretty does not fill a bed.

**Rina**  
We are offering you a hill, Edda.

**Edda**  
You are offering my grandchildren a hill in twenty-nine years. I am being asked for my compost in twenty-nine days. One of us is lending.
Nobody on the rail moved. Rina's jaw worked. Illuminara waited, and did not touch her sleeve this time.

**Illuminara**  
What would make it a loan?

**Edda**  
Weigh every tub going out, in the Garden's own log, and write it in the charter. Tonne for tonne, repaid from the hill's first cut of loam, to this bay before any ring's table. Signed by the Captain, who forgets things when he is cross.

**Rina**  
That costs the Garden its first harvest of soil.

**Edda**  
Yes. That is what makes it a loan.
Rina looked at the empty column for a long moment. Then she took out her stylus and wrote, on the back of her own hand because it was nearest, *soil owed, first page.*

**Rina**  
It goes in. And the Captain's line is in it too: the board pays whatever Ring Six writes. Soren says the board's share of the recycler's yield is four tonnes a month.
Edda ran her finger down to the sum at the foot of the first column. She did not need a pencil.

**Edda**  
Fifty-three months to clear it, and I will be dead before the middle of that.

**Rina**  
It is not the whole of it.

**Edda**  
No. It is the first line anyone has written in this column.
She wrote it herself in the second column: *Owed by the board, 212. From the first, four a month.* Beside it, in her small square hand, she added *not enough,* and did not underline it.

**Edda**  
Then you will have the soil. You will not have my watch on your hill. Somebody on this ship has to be the people who stay in the bay, or nobody keeps the soil. Don't ask them to climb. You would be asking them to forgive twice.

**Illuminara**  
I won't ask.

scenes.title: The Drift
paragraphs: *The apron face and the Ring One gantry · the day of the drift, 11:10*

They laid the first lift in nine days, the second in nine, and the third in ten, which was one day too many. The crews that had stood in the rack for fourteen months stood on the apron with cutting bars and sods, in suits that had not been out of storage since the Refusal's centenary. Some came because Rina's ring had voted. Some came because Mato's crew had. Some came because the work had a name, and the name was somewhere to sit.
The Hollow Watch did not come. Their soil came up the lock in sealed tubs, each chalked with its weight in Edda's square hand, and every sod on the apron lay on a hand's depth of it.

The drift arrived at 11:10 on the forty-first day. At first it was nothing, a faint thickening of the dark, then a bright sheet on the apron's face that did not stop. Illuminara stood on the gantry beside Soren and watched the ship take it. Where the mats lay, grit went in and stayed in, and the ice beneath did not feel it. Where the old plate was thin, it did.

**Soren**  
Section four's plate is going. Nineteen metres of old apron between the new lift and the skin, and the lift stops at the seam. The last sods are cut, cured and stacked at the lock, so the laying is all the work: three hours for one crew, under one for forty on a span this short. If they do not go on in the sheet, section four opens to the dark with seventeen people in it.

**Mato**  
This is Mato. I went below before the first sod, and sixteen others are down here with me. My deputy has the face. Say the rest, chief.

**Soren**  
The face crews have to lay them in the blizzard, on a plate that may not hold them. I am not ordering this. I am asking. The Captain has promised to keep off the channel.
The channel was quiet for the space of a breath. Then a voice nobody on the gantry knew said *Send them,* and another said it, and Soren stopped counting.
Then a slower voice came on, one Illuminara knew. The Captain had kept off the channel exactly as long as he had promised.

**Dalca**  
Chief, this is Dalca. I am not giving an order. Whatever the plate does, the board's reserve feeds every face crew and its household for forty days, and no card on this ship has a number on it until the drift is past. Every ration goes into Edda's column with the rest. It is not wages for the laying. It is mine to give.
A woman's voice answered from the face. *We were already moving, Captain. Write it in Edda's column anyway.*

**Illuminara**  
The plate has to hold the sods and the crews for as long as it takes to lay them. I can hold section four from inside. One hour. Not an hour and ten.

**Mato**  
What does the hour cost you?

**Illuminara**  
Three days of being no use to anyone. I would rather tell you now than have you plan around an hour I do not have.

**Mato**  
Then you will have it counted. Come in.

She went down the ladder into section four and put her back to the bulkhead and both hands on the plate. Sixteen people sat on the deck around her in their suits and did not look at the ceiling. The load ran down through her, huge and quiet, and she did not bargain with it. Mato stood by the seam with a hand on the cold weld and counted the minutes aloud, not loudly, the way someone had once counted passes for a child of nine holding a torch.

**Mato**  
Twelve. Hold.

**Illuminara**  
Holding.

Outside, forty people laid knit sod in a sheet of grit, one on top of another, on a plate that shook under their boots. Soren read the face off the deputy's channel as it closed: *Sod down at the seam. Sod down. Sod down.* At minute forty-eight a mat caught a slab of ice the size of a kitchen table and did not give.

**Mato**  
Fifty-one. They are sealed.

Illuminara let go with nine minutes to spare. She slid down the bulkhead and sat on the deck, her hands open on her knees. Seventeen faces looked down at her, and not one of them was looking at the ceiling.

The drift went on past them for six more days. It took sections nine and eleven of the old plate and no one with them; section four held. Where the kept hill lay under the sheet the mat held, and the ice beneath it was whole when the grit thinned. Soren put the radio down and sat on the deck, and for the first time since she had met him he held nothing at all.

scenes.title: Somewhere to Sit
paragraphs: *The Meridian rise, first lift · forty days after the drift, 09:00*
Rina was on her knees in the regolith with a sedge plug between her teeth, arguing about spacing with a boy of twelve, when the girl at the top of the path said, to nobody, that the row was crooked.

**Rina**  
Fifty metres of rise, a path, and a critic.

She took the plug out of her teeth and pushed it into the soil with her thumb, pressed the earth down once, and sat back. It was an unremarkable thing to do. The plug was the size of a coin. In ten years it would be a clump. In thirty it would be somebody's grass.

**Rina**  
Twenty-nine years. I will be seventy-four, if I am lucky, and I know exactly how lucky that is. They want to call it the Meridian. The middle of the crossing. I told them it was a ridiculous name for a hill.

**Illuminara**  
It is the right size for it.

**Mato**  
They call the top the Bench. Don't ask me who started that.

Below them the first tubs from the Hollow Watch stood in a row at the foot of the path, each chalked with its weight, and beside them the Garden's log lay open on a crate to its first page, with the word *Owed* at the head of a column that already had a line in it.

**Rina**  
Edda wrote the board's first four tonnes into her second column on the first of the month. She says it is the first line and it is not enough. The Watch lent us soil and not one hand, and I have not decided what I think about that.

**Illuminara**  
You don't have to yet.

Rina took another plug from her pocket. A man was climbing the path, slowly, without the gold on his collar, with a brass valve handle in a cloth bag held in front of him like something that might spill. Captain Dalca stopped halfway up, out of breath, and looked at the girl on the Bench as one looks at a rule one has not met.

**Dalca**  
Is there a rule about who sits where?
The girl considered the question seriously.

**Girl**  
No.

He climbed the rest of the way and sat, heavily, at the far end, with the bag in his lap. He did not take the valve out. After a while he set the whole bag down beside him, a quarter-turn from where he had put it, and said nothing.

Illuminara climbed the path with her blistered hands in her pockets and asked if she might sit. The girl moved over six inches, which on a ship is a treaty. Below them the crews laid out the next row of plugs, arguing about spacing, and nobody was looking for her. Illuminara sat down on top of a thing that was not finished and would not be for twenty-nine years, and for once let herself be of no use to anyone.

critic_line: She finds that a ship's refusal is a grief with a ledger, and builds the hill that lets the people in the middle of the crossing choose to hold the hull before anyone asks them to.

shared_strengths: It's a warm generation-ship story built on ideas, with a striking central image: spent shield mass kept as a hill instead of thrown away. The negotiation scenes are vivid, especially the valve and Edda's empty ledger column. The middle runs heavy on logistics and charter clauses, which may slow some readers, and the drift climax feels a little predictable. The ending lands quietly and earns its place.

The story transforms an existential engineering crisis into an emotionally resonant exploration of dignity, agency, and intergenerational obligation. Mato's hill, Edda's ledger, and the Captain's valve provide memorable concrete symbols. Earned cooperation replaces simplistic heroism, and the ending beautifully resolves the central theme. Dense logistical negotiations may slow some readers, but the emotional payoff is unusually strong.

translation_sl.title: GENERACIJA, KI JE BILA ZGOLJ VMES
translation_sl.deck: Long Vesper je dvesto šest let na štiristoletni poti, ljudje, ki jo ohranjajo pri življenju, pa so nehali storiti karkoli več od najnujnejšega. Oblak drobirja je oddaljen enainštirideset dni. Illuminara najprej oddela osovražene izmene, šele nato karkoli prosi.
translation_sl.shape: Osem prizorov v enainštiridesetih dneh in jutro zatem: propadajoči predščit, šest izmen v drobirju, zaslišanje v zborni dvorani, noč v vzdrževalnem oddelku, kapitanov dnevni salon, kompostni oddelek, ki vodi knjigo dolgov, dan prihoda oblaka in hrib s klopjo.

scenes.title: Scour
paragraphs: *Long Vesper, Ring One, ploščad Scour · enainštirideset dni pred oblakom drobirja, 06:00 po ladijskem času*

Prah je že dvesto šest let brusil sprednji del ladje in to se je poznalo po tem, kako je vodja vzdrževanja prečkal ploščad: previdno, kakor da bi tla lahko imela svoje mnenje. Soren Kalu je bil suh mož v kombinezonu, na kolenih že povsem pobeljenem, tablico pa je stiskal k prsim, kakor ljudje pestujejo nekaj, kar je bilo bolno.

Pod razglednim oknom se je razprostiral predščit, kilometer široka plošča iz ledu in sintrane kamnine, ki je potovala pred ladjo in prestrezala vse, kar je vanjo metala tema. Po načrtih naj bi bil debel trideset metrov. V delovni svetlobi jih je imel devetnajst.

**Soren**  
Enainštirideset dni. Pas ledu in drobirja, širok za teden poti, nam bo s polno hitrostjo prečkal smer. Odprl bo Ring One, Ring Two in Ring Three temi: enajst tisoč ljudi. V mojih ekipah za trup jih je štiristo dvanajst in štirinajst mesecev opravljajo samo najnujnejše. Niti ene plošče več.

**Illuminara**  
Si jih vprašal?

**Soren**  
Vprašal sem. Ukazal sem. Rečejo *da, šef,* plošča pa ostane na stojalu.

**Illuminara**  
En odsek trupa lahko podpiram eno uro, če vem, kje, in ne bom se pretvarjala, da zmorem kaj več. Kilometrskega predščita ne morem držati enainštirideset noči in generacije ne morem prisiliti, da bi ji bilo mar za kraj, ki ga ne bo nikoli videla. Rada bi vedela, za kaj pa ji je mar.

**Soren**  
Ničesar ti ne bodo povedali. Tako zveni štirinajst mesecev.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne bom začela z vprašanji. Katero izmeno najbolj sovražijo?

**Soren**  
Zunanjo ploskev predščita. Enajst ur zunaj, z ročnim orodjem izpraskavati vdolbine iz ledu. Žrebamo.

**Illuminara**  
Vpiši me v razpored pod istimi pogoji kot vse druge. Sprejela bom, kar mi bo namenil žreb.
Soren jo je pogledal, kakor da bi ga prosila, naj uro navije nazaj. Nato je s svinčnikom ob rob razporeda zapisal njeno ime.

scenes.title: Šest izmen
paragraphs: *Zunanja ploskev predščita, zunanja zračna zapora Two · osemintrideset dni pred oblakom drobirja, tretja izmena*

Do tretje izmene so se ji rokavice na palcih že predrle in orodju se je nehala opravičevati. Drobir je sikal čez njen vizir kot dež po pločevinasti strehi. Strgala je, se pomaknila, pa spet strgala, po meter ledu naenkrat, za Mato Ibarra, varilko in vodjo ekipe, nizko in čokato, s podlakti kot jeklenice. Na tej ploskvi je delala dvajset let, Illuminari pa je doslej namenila štiri besede. *Levo. Niže. Ne. Znova.* Njena ekipa je naredila, kar je pisalo v razporedu, in ko se je izmena končala, so odšli domov.
V četrti uri je spoj popustil.

Zakrpna plošča, velika kot vrata, položena pred dvema generacijama, se je odtrgala od starega zvara z zvokom, ki ga je Illuminara začutila v zobeh. Za njo je bila zunanja oplata Ring One, za njo pa hodnik, kjer je spalo sto ljudi. Trije člani ekipe so planili k robovom plošče. Mato je šla k zvaru.

Illuminara je položila obe dlani na ploščo in pustila, da je obremenitev stekla skoznjo, po rokah navzdol v ogrodje, kakor je nekoč držala odprt prehod med dvema bivališčema. Bilo je majhno, težko in natančno opravilo, pa si ni govorila, da je majhno. Plošča se je nehala premikati. Mato je pokleknila pod njo, ne da bi pogledala, s prstom v rokavici zdrsela vzdolž popuščenega spoja in na otip našla stari zvar, kakor pianist v temi najde pravo tipko.

**Mato**  
Tretji prehod je hladen. Nekdo ga je položil prehitro. Drži.

**Illuminara**  
Držim.
Trajalo je štiri minute. Ko je bil novi zvar narejen, je Mato sedla nazaj na pete in dolgo gledala ploščo.

**Mato**  
Moja mati je popravila ta spoj pri štiriinštiridesetih. Jaz sem jih imela devet. Držala sem gorilnik. Del mene si je želel, da bi zdržal.
Ni se zahvalila. Illuminari je vrnila strgalo.

Do šeste izmene je Illuminara enajstim vodjem ekip ob čaju iz termovke pri zračni zapori zastavila isto vprašanje: *Če vam ne bi bilo treba vzdrževati te poti, kaj bi zgradili?* Deset jih jo je pogledalo, kakor da bi bila kruta. Enajsta je bila Mato.

**Mato**  
Hrib.

**Illuminara**  
Hrib?

**Mato**  
Nekaj, kar zraste, ko ga pustiš pri miru. Moja teta ima koze na jaloviščih za Ring Seven. Šaš preplete prah in iztrebke v preprogo, na kateri lahko poskakuješ, in vsako leto je kup malo večji. Ni še prst. Je nekaj, kar bi prst bila, če bi jo kdo pustil pri miru. Ta led strgamo vsak dan in vsak dan je isti led. Rada bi imela na tej ladji eno samo stvar, ki je bo jutri več, kot je je danes. Rada bi sedela na njej.

**Mato**  
Ne povej delegatom. Iz tega bodo naredili predlog sklepa.
Illuminara je imela dlani ožuljene skozi dve plasti rokavic in tiho se je smejala temu, da jo je prekosila varilka. Tako dobro se ni počutila že mesec dni. Ni se ustavila, da bi se vprašala, zakaj.

scenes.title: Zbor
paragraphs: *Ring Four, zborna dvorana · triintrideset dni pred oblakom drobirja, 19:00*
Štiristo ljudi je napolnilo dvorano in tribune nad njo, in med kapitanovim govorom nihče ni spustil niti glasu.

Imre Dalca je bil star šestdeset let, suh in vzravnan, z zlatimi ladijskimi oznakami na že zmehčanem ovratniku. Bral je z lista. Od prvega v mesecu bodo ure dela na trupu vezane na kartice za obroke: vsaki ekipi, ki ne bo dosegla norme, bodo odvzeli desetino pripadajoče hrane, dokler norme ne bo izpolnila. Oblak drobirja je resničen, je dejal, prav tako zakon, in na ladji lahko molk enega človeka pomeni smrt drugega.
Nihče ni zavpil. To je Illuminara opazila. Štiristo ljudi je sedelo z rokami v naročju in ga gledalo z vljudno praznino ljudi, ki so se že odločili.
Tedaj je v drugi vrsti tribun vstala Rina Okonkwo-Wells. Delegatka Ring Four je bila stara petinštirideset let, širokih ramen, njen glas pa je bil orodje, ki ga je uporabljala kot zidarsko žlico.

**Rina**  
Kapitan, ukaz smo slišali. Smem namesto vas nekaj vprašati vašo gostjo?

**Dalca**  
Beseda je vaša.

**Rina**  
Na zunanji ploskvi predščita je oddelala šest izmen. Moj bratranec je bil v tretji in pravi, da obiskovalka drži ploščo, kot da misli resno. Zato bom njo vprašala nekaj, česar vas ne morem. Hočete, da tvegamo roke za ljudi na planetu, ki ga nikoli ne bomo videli. Kdo pa je kdaj zgradil kaj, kamor bi lahko prispeli mi?
Illuminara je spoznala, da nima pripravljenega odgovora, in razumela, da ji je nekdo prvič v mesecu dni zastavil pošteno vprašanje.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče. Mislim, da res nihče.
Po tribunah je šel val, skoraj smeh.

**Illuminara**  
Rodili ste se med odhodom, o katerem niste odločali, in prihodom, ki ga ne boste doživeli. Z lastnimi rokami že dvesto let ohranjate to ladjo pri življenju, pa tudi tega ni nihče nikamor zapisal. Mislim, da ne odklanjate dela. Mislim, da odklanjate delo, ki v enem samem življenju nima ciljne črte.

**Rina**  
To je govor. Govorov sem se naposlušala. Kaj boš naredila s tem?

**Illuminara**  
Vprašala bom. Enajst vodij ekip sem vprašala, kaj bi zgradili, če jim ne bi bilo treba vzdrževati te poti. Deset jih ni hotelo odgovoriti. Ena je.
Imena ni povedala. Na drugi strani dvorane je Mato Ibarra povsem otrpnila.

**Rina**  
Potem ti dam tole. Tri dni. Najdi mi nekaj, kar lahko enaintridesetletnica začne in šestdesetletnica dokonča, pa bom predlog dala svojemu obroču. Če ti ne uspe, boš ti mojemu ljudstvu pojasnjevala oblak drobirja. Od njega tega ne bodo poslušali.

**Dalca**  
Če pa ji ne uspe, delegatka, bom ukaz uveljavil.

**Rina**  
Potem bova oba nekaj izvedela o tej ladji, kapitan.

scenes.title: Tone
paragraphs: *Vzdrževalni oddelek Nine · enaintrideset dni pred oblakom drobirja, 02:10*

Mato je prišla v oddelek opolnoči, z listom razporeda, prepognjenim na štiri, in v cunjo zavito kepo v žepu kombinezona. List je pogladila na Sorenovi delovni mizi. Na hrbtni strani je bila z varilskim svinčnikom narisana dolga nizka vzpetina ob boku ladje, pot, ki se je vila nanjo, in tri majhne paličaste postave na vrhu, ki so sedele.

**Soren**  
To je nasip.

**Mato**  
To je hrib.

**Soren**  
To je kup regolita, na katerem nič ne raste. Kam bi ga dali? Kdo bi ga znosil tja? V tridesetih dneh?

**Illuminara**  
Soren. Iz česa je predščit?

**Soren**  
Iz ledu in sintrane kamnine, položene v meter debelih plasteh. Vsakih štirideset let ekipe odstranijo, kar je prah obrabil, in položijo nove plasti, izrabljene pa odvržejo čez krov. Preberi dnevnik. Najbolj dolgočasen dokument na ladji je.

Ni ga prebrala. Izročil ji ga je s pomilovanjem, ki ga je prihranil za radovedneže, in brala ga je stoje. *Izrabljeni predščit, leto 120: enaintrideset tisoč ton. Leto 160: štiriintrideset. Odstranitev: vesolje.* Stolpec številk, ki se je vsakič končal z isto besedo.

**Illuminara**  
To je masa hriba. Vsakih štirideset let ta ladja postavi hrib in ga zavrže. Kaj če bi naslednjo plast položili kot hrib in jo obdržali?
Strmel je vanjo. Nato je Mato brez vprašanja izmaknil svinčnik iz prstov in začel pisati ob risbi: tone, plasti, globina udarca.

**Soren**  
Razsuti regolit odnaša kot suh rečni breg. Potrebovali bi vezivo.

**Mato**  
Rušo.

**Soren**  
Kaj?
Mato je odvila cunjo. V njej je ležal za knjigo velik kvadrat prepletenega šaša, odrezan s tetinega kupa, s spodnje strani temen klobučevinast preplet korenin.

**Mato**  
Odrežeš ga s koreninami vred, za dlan debelo. Preproga je mreža. Drobir se vanjo ujame in ne pride več ven.

Soren je kvadrat deset minut držal v curku puhalnika nad delovno mizo in ga vrtel, medtem ko je vanj pihalo drobir iz zbiralnika pod ploščadjo. Nato ga je stehtal na namizni tehtnici in za tri vdihe obmolknil.

**Soren**  
Ničesar ni izgubil. Plošči bi odneslo površinsko plast. Trije nanosi, vsak po devet ali deset dni, pod vsako rušo za dlan komposta, da korenine sežejo v globino v nekaj dneh, ne šele v več sezonah. Ruše odrežemo in pripravimo vnaprej, pred vsakim nanosom, tako da jih je treba na predščitu samo položiti. Led iz rezerve Ring Five. Kompost iz edinih dveh krajev na ladji s pravo prstjo, žitnih oddelkov Ring Five in Ring Six. Šest odstotkov obrokov za tri sezone, potem pa se bo vsako leto izboljševal, česar ni zmogel še noben predščit iz plošč.

**Illuminara**  
Kdo odloča o oddelkih?

**Soren**  
Five. Six. In kapitanov odbor za obroke, ki si je to prst že kdaj izposodil.
Pogledala je tri paličaste postave na hribu. Našla je obliko rešitve, pa z njo ni mogla ničesar; vsak njen del je pripadal nekomu drugemu, ki bi ga moral dati.

**Illuminara**  
Potem še ni moja. To je Matina risba in tvoj izračun. Pripada ljudem, ki bodo zanjo plačali.

scenes.title: Ladja, ki glasuje
paragraphs: *Kapitanov dnevni salon, Ring Two · trideset dni pred oblakom drobirja, 08:00*

Dalca jih je sprejel stoje. Illuminara je prosila za sestanek z Rino ob sebi, on pa je privolil z obrazom človeka, ki požira nekaj, kar bi najraje poslal nazaj. Na pisalni mizi je na majhnem podstavku stal star medeninast ročaj ventila, brez oznake.
Rina je razgrnila načrt hriba. Soren je razgrnil izračune ton. Kapitan ju je poslušal brez prekinjanja in na koncu sedel.

**Dalca**  
Vrt. Ukažem, naj obnovijo ščit, vi pa mi prinesete vrt.

**Rina**  
Prinašamo vam ščit, ki je tudi vrt, kapitan. Tone so iste.

**Dalca**  
In ko bo svet kakšnega obroča dvajseti dan izglasoval konec polaganja, ker na poroki nekoga dežuje? Ladja, ki glasuje o svojem ščitu, je ladja, ki lahko izglasuje, da ga sploh ne bo imela.
Rina je odprla usta. Illuminara se je narahlo dotaknila njenega rokava in Rina jih je spet zaprla.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj je ta ventil?
Dalca je pogledal medenino, kakor da je pozabil, da je tam.

**Dalca**  
Ring Three, leto sto enaintrideset. Odklonitev. Prepir o deležih vode in posadka obroča je za šest dni ustavila cikel čistilnikov zraka, da bi dokazala svoje. Devetnajst ljudi v zgornjih nadstropjih je umrlo zaradi pomanjkanja zraka, še preden je glasovanje doseglo spodnja. Moja babica je bila med njimi. To je ventil, ki so jim ga ukazali obrniti, pa ga niso. Na mizi ga imam zato, da mi nikomur ni treba razlagati, kako je videti ladja, ki reče ne.
Nihče ni spregovoril.

**Illuminara**  
Potem se ne bojite Vmesnih. Bojite se tistega, česar ladja ne more preživeti, če to odklonijo.

**Dalca**  
Da.

**Illuminara**  
Potem to zapišite. Ne kot ukaz. Kot člen.
Rina je že vlekla pisalo iz rokava.

**Rina**  
Zrak, voda, trup. Noben svet, noben obroč, noben delegat jih ne sme ustaviti ali izglasovati njihove prekinitve. Ne zaradi prepira ne zaradi poroke. Vmesni to zapišejo v listino, vsak delegat pa podpiše. Številko iz Ring Three damo v prvo vrstico.
Dalca je prebral dvakrat. Ni bil videti olajšan. Videti je bil kot človek, ki so mu izročili nekaj težkega in poštenega.

**Dalca**  
In kaj dobite v zameno?

**Rina**  
Garden je naš: delo na njem, ure, razporeditev. Vaša pristojnost obsega varnost trupa, kot doslej, in preneha, ko mine nevarnost. Odbor pa si žitnih oddelkov ne prisvoji znova, ko bo naslednjič jezen.

**Dalca**  
Odbor si je iz teh oddelkov že izposojal. Ne bom se pretvarjal, da ni res. Karkoli bo Ring Six zapisal, bo odbor poplačal iz svojega deleža izplena reciklatorja, pred katerokoli mizo. S tem deležem razpolagam jaz. Vključite to.
Rina je zapisala.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa kartice?

**Dalca**  
Kartica za obroke je edini vzvod, ki ga imam in za katerega ne potrebujem nikogaršnje privolitve. Zato sem segel po njem. To je isti vzvod, ki ga je potegnila posadka Ring Three, le da sem ga jaz potegnil z druge strani. Soren. Črtaj kartice iz obračuna ur dela na trupu. Danes.

**Soren**  
Da, kapitan.
Kapitan je vstal. Dvignil je ventil in ga spet odložil, za četrt obrata zasukanega glede na prejšnji položaj.

**Dalca**  
Ni mi všeč. Podpisal bom zaradi člena o Ring Three. Ne zato, ker bi me kdo prosil, naj zaupam Vmesnim.

**Rina**  
Nismo vas prosili. Napisali smo vam nekaj, kar lahko preverite. Listina ne bo veljala, dokler je ne prebere Ring Six. Six ima drugi oddelek, in Six je Hollow Watch.

**Dalca**  
Potem pa pojdite in naj vas zavrnejo.

scenes.title: Drugi oddelek
paragraphs: *Ring Six, oddelek Two · devetindvajset dni pred oblakom drobirja, 07:40*

Hollow Watch so čakali: enajst ljudi v sivih delovnih haljah ob ograji nad kompostnimi gredami, molčečih prav na tisti način, ki pove, da so nekoč že povedali vse. V oddelku je dišalo po topli prsti, edini topli prsti na ladji. Illuminara ni vedela, kako zelo pogreša ta vonj, dokler ga ni začutila v grlu.
Za oddelek je skrbela Edda Voss. Imela je enainsedemdeset let in nosila jih je kot pas za orodje, z obema rokama pa je k rebrom stiskala papirnato knjigo evidenc.

**Rina**  
Vsi obroči razen tvojega so prebrali listino, Edda. Kapitan je rekel, da jo bo podpisal.

**Edda**  
Prebrala sem jo. Piše, da odbor ne sme vzeti oddelkov nazaj, kadar je jezen. Ne piše pa, kdo jih bo vrnil, ko boste končali.

**Rina**  
Nihče ničesar ne jemlje. To je posojilo.

**Edda**  
Ali res. Pridi sem, tujka.
Odprla je knjigo na ograji. Po vsaki strani sta tekla dva stolpca, zapisana najprej z isto roko, nato z mlajšo in nazadnje z njeno.

**Edda**  
Prst je edino, česar ta ladja ne more izdelati. Ustvarimo jo tako, da devetdeset let pustimo stvarem razpadati v temi. Štirikrat so prišli po celo sezonsko zalogo: za trup leta sto petnajst; za reaktorski ščit; za vodovod; v letu, ko je pridelek napadla bolezen. Vsakič so bili prosilci prestrašeni in razlog dober, tona je šla skozi zračno zaporo, jaz pa sem jo zapisala sem. Posojeno, dvesto dvanajst ton. Tale stolpec pa je za tisto, kar se je vrnilo.
Drugi stolpec je bil prazen od vrha strani do dna.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj si še naprej posojala?

**Edda**  
Ker je dolg, ki ga nihče ne zabeleži, darilo, za darilo, ki ga nisi bila niti naprošena dati, pa se ti nihče ne zahvali.
Illuminara je pomislila na dnevnik predščita, v katerem se je vsak stolpec končal z eno samo besedo. Sorenova ladja je odmetavala maso, ne da bi jo poimenovala. Edda jo je posojala brez imena.

**Illuminara**  
V kapitanovem dnevniku se vsaka vrstica konča z *vesolje.* V tvojem se ne konča z ničimer. To je isti stolpec.

**Edda**  
Lepo. A lepota ne napolni grede.

**Rina**  
Ponujamo ti hrib, Edda.

**Edda**  
Mojim vnukom ponujate hrib čez devetindvajset let. Od mene pa terjate kompost v devetindvajsetih dneh. Ena od nas posoja.
Nihče ob ograji se ni premaknil. Rini so se napenjale čeljusti. Illuminara je počakala in tokrat se ni dotaknila njenega rokava.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi bilo potrebno, da bi to postalo posojilo?

**Edda**  
Stehtajte vsako posodo, ki gre ven, zapišite jo v lastno knjigo Gardna in v listino. Tono za tono povrnete iz prvega pridelka prsti na hribu, v ta oddelek, pred mizo kateregakoli obroča. Podpiše kapitan, ki rad pozabi, kadar je jezen.

**Rina**  
Garden bo tako ostal brez prvega pridelka prsti.

**Edda**  
Da. Zato je to posojilo.
Rina je dolgo gledala prazni stolpec. Nato je izvlekla pisalo in na hrbtno stran lastne dlani, ker je bila najbliže, zapisala *dolgovana prst, prva stran.*

**Rina**  
To gre noter. In tudi kapitanova vrstica je že tam: odbor plača, karkoli bo zapisal Ring Six. Soren pravi, da odboru pripadajo štiri tone izplena reciklatorja na mesec.
Edda je s prstom zdrsnila do vsote ob vznožju prvega stolpca. Svinčnika ni potrebovala.

**Edda**  
Triinpetdeset mesecev, da se dolg poravna, jaz pa bom mrtva, še preden bo polovica tega mimo.

**Rina**  
To ni vse.

**Edda**  
Ne. Je pa to prva vrstica, ki jo je kdo kadarkoli zapisal v ta stolpec.
Sama jo je vpisala v drugi stolpec: *Odbor dolguje 212. Od začetka po štiri na mesec.* Ob njej je s svojo drobno oglato pisavo dodala *premalo,* ne da bi besedo podčrtala.

**Edda**  
Potem boste dobili prst. Moje straže pa na vašem hribu ne bo. Nekdo na tej ladji mora biti med tistimi, ki ostanejo v oddelku, sicer nihče ne ohrani prsti. Ne prosite jih, naj se povzpnejo. Prosili bi jih, naj odpustijo dvakrat.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom jih prosila.

scenes.title: Oblak drobirja
paragraphs: *Zunanja ploskev predščita in ploščad Ring One · na dan prihoda oblaka, 11:10*

Prvi nanos so položili v devetih dneh, drugega v devetih in tretjega v desetih, kar je bilo za dan preveč. Ekipe, ki so štirinajst mesecev stale ob stojalih, so zdaj stale na predščitu z rezalnimi palicami in kosi ruše, v skafandrih, ki jih niso vzeli iz skladišča vse od stoletnice Odklonitve. Nekateri so prišli, ker je Rinin obroč glasoval. Nekateri zato, ker je glasovala Matina ekipa. Nekateri zato, ker je delo imelo ime in je to ime pomenilo kraj, kjer je mogoče sedeti.

Hollow Watch niso prišli. Njihova prst je prihajala skozi zračno zaporo v zapečatenih posodah, na vsaki je bila z Eddino oglato pisavo s kredo zapisana teža, in vsak kos ruše na predščitu je ležal na za dlan globoki plasti te prsti.

Oblak je prispel ob 11:10 na enainštirideseti dan. Sprva ni bilo ničesar, le tema se je neznatno zgostila, nato pa je na sprednjo ploskev predščita udarila svetla zavesa, ki ni ponehala. Illuminara je stala na ploščadi ob Sorenu in gledala, kako jo ladja sprejema. Kjer so ležale preproge, se je drobir ujel vanje in ostal tam, led pod njimi pa ga ni čutil. Kjer je bila stara plošča tanka, ga je.

**Soren**  
Plošča v odseku štiri popušča. Med novim nanosom in oplato je devetnajst metrov starega predščita, nanos pa se konča pri spoju. Zadnje kose ruše smo odrezali, utrdili in naložili pri zapori, tako da jih je treba samo še položiti: tri ure za eno ekipo, manj kot eno uro za štirideset ljudi na tako kratkem odseku. Če jih ne položijo sredi te zavese, se bo odsek štiri odprl temi, v njem pa je sedemnajst ljudi.

**Mato**  
Tukaj Mato. Še pred prvo rušo sem šla dol in šestnajst drugih je tukaj z mano. Moja namestnica vodi zunanjo ploskev. Povej še ostalo, šef.

**Soren**  
Zunanje ekipe jih morajo polagati v metežu, na ploščo, ki jih morda ne bo zdržala. Tega ne ukazujem. Prosim. Kapitan je obljubil, da se ne bo oglasil na kanalu.
Na kanalu je za en vdih zavladala tišina. Nato je glas, ki ga na ploščadi ni poznal nihče, rekel *Pošljite jih,* in za njim še eden, in Soren je nehal šteti.
Potem se je oglasil počasnejši glas, ki ga je Illuminara poznala. Kapitan je ostal zunaj kanala natanko toliko časa, kolikor je obljubil.

**Dalca**  
Vodja, tukaj Dalca. Ne izdajam ukaza. Karkoli se bo zgodilo s ploščo, bo odborova rezerva štirideset dni hranila vse ekipe z zunanje ploskve in njihove družine, in dokler oblak ne mine, na nobeni kartici za obroke na tej ladji ne bo številke. Vsak obrok gre skupaj z ostalim v Eddin stolpec. To ni plačilo za polaganje. To lahko dam sam.
Ženski glas z zunanje ploskve je odgovoril: *Mi smo se že premaknili, kapitan. Vseeno zapišite v Eddin stolpec.*

**Illuminara**  
Plošča mora zdržati rušo in ekipe toliko časa, da jo položijo. Odsek štiri lahko držim od znotraj. Eno uro. Ne ure in deset minut.

**Mato**  
Kaj te ta ura stane?

**Illuminara**  
Tri dni, ko ne bom nikomur v korist. Raje ti povem zdaj, kot da bi načrtovala s časom, ki ga nimam.

**Mato**  
Potem bomo to upoštevali. Pridi noter.

Po lestvi se je spustila v odsek štiri, se s hrbtom uprla ob pregrado in obe dlani položila na ploščo. Šestnajst ljudi je v skafandrih sedelo na tleh okoli nje in ni gledalo v strop. Skoznjo je stekla obremenitev, ogromna in tiha, in z njo se ni pogajala. Mato je stala ob spoju z dlanjo na hladnem zvaru in na glas štela minute, a ne glasno, kakor je nekoč nekdo štel prehode devetletnemu otroku, ki je držal gorilnik.

**Mato**  
Dvanajst. Drži.

**Illuminara**  
Držim.

Zunaj je štirideset ljudi v zavesi drobirja polagalo prepleteno rušo, kos za kosom, na ploščo, ki se jim je tresla pod škornji. Soren je poslušal poročila namestnice z zunanje ploskve, ko so zapirali vrzel: *Ruša pri spoju položena. Ruša položena. Ruša položena.* V oseminštirideseti minuti je preproga ujela kos ledu, velik kot kuhinjska miza, in ni popustila.

**Mato**  
Enainpetdeset. Zatesnili so.

Illuminara je popustila devet minut pred iztekom. Zdrsnila je po pregradi navzdol in obsedela na tleh, dlani je imela odprte na kolenih. Sedemnajst obrazov je gledalo vanjo in niti eden ni gledal v strop.

Oblak drobirja jih je bičal še šest dni. Odnesel je odseka devet in enajst stare plošče, vendar z njima ni odnesel nikogar; odsek štiri je zdržal. Kjer je pod zaveso ležal ohranjeni hrib, je preproga zdržala, led pod njo pa je ostal cel, ko se je drobir razredčil. Soren je odložil radijsko postajo in sedel na tla. Prvič, odkar ga je poznala, ni držal prav ničesar.

scenes.title: Kraj, kjer se lahko usedeš
paragraphs: *Vzpetina Meridian, prvi nanos · štirideset dni po oblaku drobirja, 09:00*
Rina je klečala v regolitu s čepičem šaša med zobmi in se prepirala o razmikih z dvanajstletnim fantom, ko je deklica na vrhu poti, ne da bi govorila komu posebej, pripomnila, da je vrsta postrani.

**Rina**  
Petdeset metrov vzpetine, pot in kritičarka.

Čepič je vzela iz ust in ga s palcem potisnila v prst, enkrat pritisnila zemljo okoli njega in sedla nazaj. Nič posebnega ni bilo na tem. Čepič je bil velik kot kovanec. Čez deset let bo šop. Čez trideset bo to nekogaršnja trava.

**Rina**  
Devetindvajset let. Imela jih bom štiriinsedemdeset, če bom imela srečo, in prav dobro vem, koliko sreče bi za to potrebovala. Hočejo mu reči Meridian. Sredina poti. Povedala sem jim, da je to smešno ime za hrib.

**Illuminara**  
Ravno pravšnje velikosti je zanj.

**Mato**  
Vrhu pravijo Bench. Ne sprašuj me, kdo je začel.

Pod njimi so ob vznožju poti v vrsti stale prve posode Hollow Watch, vsaka s kredo zapisano težo. Poleg njih je na zaboju ležala odprta knjiga Gardna, na prvi strani, z besedo *Dolgovano* na vrhu stolpca, v katerem je bila že ena vrstica.

**Rina**  
Edda je prve štiri tone odborovega vračila v drugi stolpec zapisala prvega v mesecu. Pravi, da je to prva vrstica in da ni dovolj. Straža nam je posodila prst, ne pa ene same roke, in še nisem odločena, kaj si mislim o tem.

**Illuminara**  
Še ni treba.

Rina je iz žepa vzela nov čepič. Po poti se je počasi vzpenjal moški, brez zlatih oznak na ovratniku, z medeninastim ročajem ventila v platneni vreči, ki jo je nosil pred seboj, kot bi se iz nje lahko kaj razlilo. Kapitan Dalca je zadihan obstal na polovici poti in pogledal deklico na Bench, kakor človek pogleda pravilo, s katerim se še ni srečal.

**Dalca**  
Ali obstaja pravilo, kdo sme kje sedeti?
Deklica je vprašanje resno premislila.

**Deklica**  
Ne.

Prehodil je še preostanek poti in težko sedel na skrajni konec, z vrečo v naročju. Ventila ni vzel iz nje. Čez čas je celo vrečo položil poleg sebe, za četrt obrata zasukano glede na prejšnji položaj, in ni rekel ničesar.

Illuminara se je s požuljenimi rokami v žepih povzpela po poti in vprašala, ali sme prisesti. Deklica se je pomaknila za šest palcev, kar je na ladji že mirovna pogodba. Pod njimi so ekipe razporejale naslednjo vrsto čepičev in se prepirale o razmikih, nje pa ni iskal nihče. Illuminara je sedla na nekaj, kar še ni bilo dokončano in še devetindvajset let ne bo, in si je enkrat za spremembo dovolila, da nikomur ni v korist.

translation_sl.critic_line: Ugotovi, da je ladijsko odklanjanje žalost s knjigo dolgov, in zgradi hrib, zaradi katerega se ljudje sredi poti sami odločijo podpreti ladijski trup, še preden jih kdo prosi za to.

late_publication.reason: Published later, on 18 November 2026, by BD's decision. The GPT scheduled tasks were out of usage on 17 November, so the 21:00 day freeze was never created and the nightly publisher could not run. The stories were completed and closed on 17 November; Claude also reviewed and closed S2 and S3 as a recorded stand-in for GPT. The original Claude reader files were unusable (a storage-format error), so both reader scores were made afterwards, after the 20:30 cutoff, by fresh isolated readers (GPT in a ChatGPT chat, Claude in a sandboxed one-shot call); the Slovenian translations of S2 and S3 were made later in ChatGPT chats.
late_publication.reason_sl: Objavljeno naknadno, 18. novembra 2026, po BD-jevi odločitvi. GPT-naloge 17. novembra zaradi omejitve porabe niso tekle, zato zamrznitev dneva ob 21:00 ni nastala in nočni objavljalnik ni mogel teči. Zgodbe so bile dokončane in zaključene 17. novembra; Claude je zgodbi S2 in S3 tudi pregledal in zaključil kot zapisano nadomestilo za GPT. Prvotne Claudove bralske datoteke so bile neuporabne (napaka v obliki zapisa), zato sta obe bralski oceni nastali pozneje, po rezu ob 20:30, pri svežih izoliranih bralcih (GPT v klepetu ChatGPT, Claude v peščenem enkratnem klicu); slovenska prevoda zgodb S2 in S3 sta nastala pozneje v klepetih ChatGPT.
